            (B) 
by striking out “15% ad val.” in each of items 470.23 and 470.65 and inserting in lieu thereof “Free”;
 
            (C) 
by striking out “6% ad val.” and “15% ad val.” in item 470.25 and inserting in lieu thereof “Free”;
 
            (D) 
by striking out “2.5% ad val.” and “15% ad val.” in item 470.55 and inserting in lieu thereof “Free”; and
 
            (E) 
by striking out “3.5% ad val.” and “15% ad val.” in item 470.57 and inserting in lieu thereof “Free”.
  
        (2) Item 907.80 of the Appendix to such Schedules is repealed.
  
    (b)

        (1) 
The amendments made by subsection (a) shall apply with respect to articles entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or after the date of the enactment of this Act.
 
        (2) 
Upon request therefor filed with the customs officer concerned on or before the 90th day after the date of the enactment of this Act, the entry or withdrawal of any article described in item 907.80 of the Tariff Schedules of the United States (as in effect on June 30, 1978) and—

            (A) 
that was made after June 30, 1978, and before the date of the enactment of this Act, and
 
            (B) 
with respect to which there would have been no duty if any of the amendments made by subsection (a)(1) applied to such entry or withdrawal,
   shall, notwithstanding the provisions of section 514 of the Tariff Act of 1930 or any other provision of law, be liquidated or reliquidated as though such entry or withdrawal had been made on the date of the enactment of this Act.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that an importer's "request" filed with a customs officer is outside-party involvement in a federal decision. But that request is simply an application for a refund-type benefit (reliquidation at the new duty-free rate), which the definition excludes. The rest of the section directly amends tariff schedules by statute, with no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue.
fable.s: Upon request therefor filed with the customs officer concerned on or before the 90th day after the date of the enactment of this Act

qwen_block.w: This section amends the Tariff Schedules of the United States to change duty rates for specific items (e.g., Logwood). It does not involve consultation with, or participation by, any non-federal entities in the decision-making process. The changes are legislative mandates regarding tariff rates, not procedural requirements for public input or advisory boards.
qwen_block.s: Subpart A of part 9 of schedule 4 of the Tariff Schedules of the United States (19 U.S.C. 1202) is amended— (A) by striking out item 470.15 and inserting in lieu thereof the following: ... 470.16 Logwood Free Free ...

opus.w: This section changes tariff rates and lets importers ask for their past entries to be reliquidated. One might read "request therefor filed with the customs officer" as an outside party taking part in a federal decision. But that request is really an application for a duty refund, which is like an application for a benefit and is excluded by the definition. Nothing in the section creates consultation, a comment period, a hearing, an advisory body, or rulemaking.
opus.s: Upon request therefor filed with the customs officer concerned on or before the 90th day after the date of the enactment of this Act, the entry or withdrawal of any article described in item 907.80

qwen_chat.w: This section amends tariff schedules and provides a mechanism for importers to request retroactive application of new duty rates. The 'request' is an administrative step for individual transactions, not a consultation or coordination process involving outside parties in federal decision-making. It does not involve public comment periods, advisory committees with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes before a federal action. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Upon request therefor filed with the customs officer concerned on or before the 90th day after the date of the enactment of this Act, the entry or withdrawal of any article described in item 907.80 of the Tariff Schedules of the United States (as in effect on June 30, 1978) and— (A) that was made after June 30, 1978, and before the date of the enactment of this Act, and (B) with respect to which there would have been no duty if any of the amendments made by subsection (a)(1) applied to such entry or withdrawal, shall, notwithstanding the provisions of section 514 of the Tariff Act of 1930 or any other provision of law, be liquidated or reliquidated as though such entry or withdrawal had been made on the date of the enactment of this Act.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "request" mentioned in subsection (b)(2) constitutes participation because it involves an outside party (an importer) interacting with a federal official (the customs officer). However, this is merely an administrative procedure for applying a retroactive tariff change to a specific transaction, not a consultation or coordination process where the outside party influences a broader federal policy decision or rulemaking. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or administrative processing of individual cases from the definition of participation.
